_source: Windows Calibri's Arabic as Windows Excel prints it (lookwin p220-lw, look-win 58th), by skeleton glyph (Calibri sets a letter's dots as marks): chars maps a character to its joining type (D dual, R right, U none, C join-causing, T transparent mark) and the glyph of each joining form, and pairs[a][b] two joined glyphs set as one ligature (lam-alef, seen-reh, feh-yeh...), both weights alike; per weight (R, B), adv a glyph's advance and kern the kerning Uniscribe adds after a glyph before the next base glyph in logical order, kern[first[a]][second[b]]; font units, 2,048 an em. Excel prints each glyph at its advance plus that kerning, rounded half up to whole printer dots at the printer's ppem (p220: 808 forms at 9-14 pt, 30 sentences of R456-X32 at 11 pt within 4 dots). Metrics only, read with HarfBuzz from Office's copy of the face by lookwin tools/build_arabic_advances.py. Both ends read this file (API office_arabic_advances.json, web office-arabic-advances.json); the letters are drawn in Noto Sans Arabic spread to these widths.
